summary: Drolma is a Tibetologist who earned an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo (~2006–2008), where she studied under supervisor Hanna Havnevik.
Dror Burstein works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2014 and teaches literature at Tel Aviv University.

Duncan Forbes was an indologist and linguist who studied at Perth Grammar School and the University of St Andrews (~1818–1823). He held posts at King's College London (~1837–1861) and the British Museum (~1849–1855).

Duncan Ryūken Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Reed College (~1987–1991) and Harvard University (~1993–2000), later holding posts at UC Irvine (~2002–2006) and UC Berkeley (~2006–2011).
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed a PhD at Boston University (~1995–2001) under doctoral supervisor Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lozang Trinlé was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ngawang Yönten and at Gyuto Monastery (~1948–1951). He served at Minzu University (~1954–1965), Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (~1985–1997), and Tibet University (~1985–1997).

Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Lucknow (~-1974) under doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri, and also studied under R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.

Durgamohan Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Scottish Church College, Vidyasagar College, and the University of Calcutta (~1921–1923). He later held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1957–1965).

Dwijendra Nath Shukla was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor K. A. Subramania Iyer and earned a D.Litt. from the University of Lucknow (~-1957). He held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.
Dylan Esler is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at SOAS (~2005–2006) and a PhD at KU Leuven (~2013–2018). He served as a research scholar at KU Leuven in ~2018.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen, and was a professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University (1990–1995).

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University, and served as director of Nitartha Institute and Kamalashila Institute, and at Nalanda West.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS, learning under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Sakya Trizin, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Dörte Kamarid is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the University of Vienna (~2008–2015), where Helmut Tauscher served as MA supervisor.

E. Gene Smith was a Tibetologist who studied at Hobart and William Smith Colleges, University of Utah, and University of Washington under Turrell V. Wylie. He worked at the Library of Congress (1968–1997) and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (~1999–2010).
E. H. Johnston was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell (~1904–1908). He served as a professor at the University of Oxford from ~1937 to 1942.

E. Michael Mendelson was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed studies at King's College and the University of Cambridge (~1947–1950), the University of Paris (~1950–1953), and the University of Chicago (~1953–1956).
E. W. Adikaram was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of London (~1931–1933), where he studied under William Stede.

Eberhard Sandschneider is a sinologist who studied at Saarland University (~1974–1981). He held positions at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1998), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Edeltraud Harzer is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Charles University and the University of Washington (~-1986). She has held posts at Stanford, Indiana University, the University of Washington, University of Puget Sound, and UT Austin (1998).
